why: The arm COPIES Back into its header instead of moving it, so the pane carries two Back buttons: one in the header where it is seen, one still in the pinned bar. The clone has no listeners, so the visible control does nothing -- and the keyboard walk now closes over an extra dead stop. Every structural assertion about the header still passes; only the population of controls changes, which is why one case compares the two layouts' full control sets rather than checking the header alone.
killedBy: hud: the versus action bar and its arm (issue #668) both layouts expose the same controls -- the arm moves them, it does not add or drop any
